signals.opens: Gmail opens were {pct} of other inboxes'.
signals.mailboxFull: {pct} of mailboxes were full or inactive.
signals.complaints: {pct} of people marked it as spam.

signalsShort.opens: Gmail opens were {pct} of other inboxes'
signalsShort.mailboxFull: {pct} of mailboxes were full or inactive

rail.next: up to {count} if delivery stays healthy

row.warmingNote: Most active contacts go first. Volume grows each day delivery stays healthy.
row.doneNote: Broadcasts from this domain go out at normal speed.
row.pausedWaiting: {waiting, plural, one {# email is} other {# emails are}} waiting until you resume.
row.pausedNothing: Broadcasts from this domain wait until you resume.

off.row: Not warming up · most sent in a day so far: {count}
off.rowNote: Turn it on before a big first send from a new domain or subdomain.
off.preview: A broadcast to all {total} contacts would go out like this
off.previewActive: {eligible} active contacts in about {days, plural, one {# sending day} other {# sending days}}, most active first.
off.previewAll: {eligible} contacts in about {days, plural, one {# sending day} other {# sending days}}, most active first.
off.previewSkipped: {inactive} with no activity in 90+ days are skipped.
off.previewLast: {inactive} with no activity in 90+ days go last.
off.previewTail: Each healthy day grows the volume 1.5×. Your transactional email is never held.
off.switchHint: Big sends start small and grow each day while delivery stays healthy. Leave it off if this domain already sends this volume through another provider.

pace.label: Warm-up pace
pace.note: Each healthy day grows the volume 1.5×. One weak signal holds it, two cut it by 30%, and a severe one pauses it. Mail over the day's volume waits for the next day. Nothing is lost. Your transactional email is never held.

health.label: Delivery health · {day}

tips.opens: Gmail opens compared with other inboxes on the same send. A low share is the clearest sign Gmail is filing the mail as spam. Machine prefetches never count.
tips.mailboxFull: Mailboxes that answered full or inactive. A second answer like that stops mail to the address.
tips.complaints: Gmail doesn't tell senders about spam reports. See your spam rate in Google Postmaster Tools.

health.openTrackingOff: Turn on open tracking to see this signal.
health.footer: Gmail keeps its spam rate to itself. See it in <link>Google Postmaster Tools ↗</link>
health.pausedByTeam: Your team paused this warm-up on {date}.

settings.orderHint: Each day's volume goes to the people most likely to open it, ranked by the newest of these signals.
settings.byTransactional: Got your transactional email in the last 30 days
settings.propertyHint: Use a date, like the last login.
settings.inactiveHint: {inactive} of your {total} contacts haven't been active in 90+ days. Mailing them from a new domain is the fastest way to the spam folder.
settings.targetHint: The most you plan to send in a day. Warm-up ends after a healthy day at this volume.
settings.targetError: Use a whole number from {min} to {max}, no lower than the starting volume.
settings.startHint: Day 1 sends this many. Raise it if this domain already sends every day through another provider.
settings.startError: Use a whole number from {min} to {max}, no higher than the daily target.
settings.controlHint: Paused, mail from this domain waits until you resume. Turned off, the waiting mail goes out at normal speed.

turnOff.title: Turn off warm-up?
turnOff.bodyWaiting: {waiting, plural, one {# waiting email} other {# waiting emails}} will go out at normal speed. With {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} of history, a big day is likely to land in spam.
turnOff.body: Big sends from this domain will go out at normal speed.

paused.beforeHint: Gmail judges a new sender by how its first recipients react.
paused.whoBody: {pct} of your contacts haven't been active in 90+ days. Start again with the most active.
paused.spamBody: Gmail shows it only in Google Postmaster Tools, a day late. Above 0.3% Gmail starts rejecting mail.
paused.deadBody: Full or inactive mailboxes stop getting your mail after a second answer like that.
paused.resumeHint: Starts again at {volume} a day. The waiting mail keeps its order and is kept until {date}.

done.note: Broadcasts from this domain go out at normal speed. Turn warm-up on again if you'll send far more than {target} a day.

error: Couldn't change the warm-up. Try again.
